DEEP Robotics outlines Brain architecture across five research areas

The announcement brings together contact-aware prediction, video learning, policy improvement, revisable memory and real-robot evaluation.

GlobeNewswire ↗24 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 6

Connecting complementary research

DEEP Robotics outlined DEEPRobotics-Brain on October 24, linking world modeling, navigation and manipulation, policy improvement, memory and evaluation. The announcement explains how these components fit together; it does not imply that every underlying study originated or first appeared that day.

Physical prediction and motion learning

DR-WM-1.0 incorporates geometry and surface properties such as friction rather than relying only on plausible-looking video. DR-VLA combines human egocentric video with robot demonstrations through EgoLynx. AMC represents arm motion with 13 primitives to connect language, direction and force feedback.

Simulation and physical results differ

DR-APO reports navigation success rising from 70.33% to 89.55% in simulation and from 25% to 65% on physical LYNX M20 tests under research conditions. These are separate evaluations. DR-Agent meanwhile uses time-indexed object memory and replans as environments change.

Benchmarks do not certify deployment

DR-Benchmark uses LynxScenes, described as 833.6 hours and 3,294.7 kilometers of real operation, for perception, trajectory prediction, future scenes and reconstruction. The reported studies provide research evidence, not certification that an integrated system works everywhere or that a new commercial product is shipping.
